title: WTH: Why the Tile Card...?
text: WTH: Why the Tile Card…? Why is there no option to center the icon , when showing it without the name or description? A vertical centering option for the icon alone would also help to create icon-only dashboards. Why can’t the card be made smaller ? The minimum size currently allowed is half a column. Why is there no option to choose a color for the OFF state and for other states, depending on the entity? Right now, only the ON state can be colored, if you leave the default setting, the card automatically applies it’s own “ON” color to entities such as heating or air conditioning. Why can’t you set custom text or use YAML in the description ? This would be useful for displaying the entity’s (or another’s) own consumption in small text. Why can’t you set identical actions quickly ? Tap, hold and double-tap actions should be copied automatically from the icon to the entire card, if you assign one action, the card applies it to the other interactions by default (unless you specify otherwise). 21 posts - 5 participants Read full topic

title: Product-level volume pricing for B2B catalogs
text: TL;DR: Feature request to let catalog volume pricing apply at the product level, not just the variant level. The problem I’m exploring Shopify B2B (native B2B, not Shopify Plus) for a couple clients & have found a frustrating limitation in it’s implementation for products with multiple variants. When you set up a catalog, volume pricing discounts are based on the quantity of each variant, not the total across the product. Buyers can’t combine variants of the same product on a given order to reach a price break. That is a buyer who orders a mix of variants may never get the discount set up in the catalog. Example A candle (product) comes in three scents (variants): Vanilla, Lavender and Sandalwood. It has a 6-unit price break in the custom catalog we made for B2B customers ( B2B markets and catalogs ). A buyer orders 6 candles in total: 2x Vanilla, 2x Lavender and 2x Sandalwood. The 6-unit break never applies, because the buyer only ordered 2 of each variant. We could work around this by setting the break at 2 units, but then we can’t reward larger orders, which defeats the point of volume discounts. B2B buyers order this way all the time in client stores. If a B2B customer orders ‘X’ units of a product, every unit should (optionally) count towards the price break, no matter which variants of the product they choose. Requested solution Add a setting to each product’s volume pricing in a catalog, so the quantity for each price break can be counted per variant or per product . Something like this: In our example with the ‘count variants towards price break’ setting enabled the 6x products (3x2 variants) would trigger the discount. It would also be nice to set price breaks as percentages rather than hard-coded dollar values which are clunky to manage natively on store catalogs with lots of products/variants. Given native B2B is still relatively new (Nov 2026), there is likely a technical reason it hasn’t yet been implemented by Shopify. That said, it is a frequent pain point I see in my clients’ stores. It would be good to get an official response detailing if there are plans to solve this or recommended work arounds that don’t involve installing another app! It is hard to recommend the native B2B feature to clients with many product/variants until this is solved. If you need this too, please comment below so the B2B team can see how many merchants it affects. 1 post - 1 participant Read full topic
triage_reason: Feature request for product-level volume pricing in Shopify B2B catalogs.
